scenarios.title: Valid App Definition with Service References
scenarios.description: Verify a valid App configuration file in the top-level apps directory containing valid ServiceConsumerReference and ServiceProviderReference elements mapping to existing transport services.
scenarios.expected_result: The application configuration is successfully parsed and validated.

scenarios.title: Duplicate Application Binding in Controller
scenarios.description: Verify that defining duplicate bindings for the same application within a single controller's app_bindings.flync.yaml file is detected and rejected.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails due to duplicate application binding on the same controller.

scenarios.title: App Definition with Empty Service References
scenarios.description: Verify the boundary case where an App configuration file is defined with empty service consumer and provider reference lists.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is valid, representing an application with no transport service mappings.

scenarios.title: Valid Controller App Bindings
scenarios.description: Verify that an ECU controller successfully binds multiple valid applications defined in the top-level apps directory using app_bindings.flync.yaml.
scenarios.expected_result: The app bindings are successfully validated and associated with the controller.

scenarios.title: App Binding Referencing Non-Existent App
scenarios.description: Verify that app_bindings.flync.yaml is rejected if it references an application name that does not exist as a file in the top-level apps directory.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails due to a dangling application reference.

scenarios.title: Valid CAN Bus Configuration
scenarios.description: Test a valid CAN bus configuration containing a unique bus name, participating nodes, and inline frames referencing valid PDUs by pdu_ref.
scenarios.expected_result: The CAN bus configuration is successfully validated.

scenarios.title: Invalid Standard CAN ID Range
scenarios.description: Test a CAN bus configuration where a standard CAN frame is configured with an out-of-range ID of 2048 (maximum is 2047).
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is rejected because the standard CAN ID exceeds the 11-bit limit (0-2047).
scenarios.injected_fault: Standard CAN frame ID set to 2048

scenarios.title: CAN FD Maximum Payload Boundary
scenarios.description: Test a CAN FD bus configuration with a frame payload at the maximum boundary of 64 bytes.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is successfully validated with a 64-byte CAN FD frame payload.

scenarios.title: Valid LIN Bus Configuration
scenarios.description: Test a valid LIN bus configuration containing exactly one master node, slave nodes, and schedule tables referencing inline-defined frames.
scenarios.expected_result: The LIN bus configuration is successfully validated.

scenarios.title: LIN Bus with Multiple Master Nodes
scenarios.description: Test a LIN bus configuration containing more than one master node, violating the single-master rule.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is rejected because a LIN bus must have exactly one master node.
scenarios.injected_fault: Configuring two master nodes on a single LIN bus

scenarios.title: LIN Bus Maximum Slave Nodes Boundary
scenarios.description: Test a LIN bus configuration with the maximum limit of 16 slave nodes.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is successfully validated with exactly 16 slave nodes.

scenarios.title: Valid TCP Profile Configuration with Standard Options
scenarios.description: Verify that a TCP profile defined in tcp_profiles.flync.yaml with valid TCPOption parameters (such as a valid port within the 1024-65535 range and standard keep-alive options) is successfully parsed and validated.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is parsed successfully without errors, and the TCP profile is correctly registered.

scenarios.title: Invalid TCP Port Option Value
scenarios.description: Verify that defining a TCP profile with an invalid port number (e.g., 70000, which exceeds the maximum 16-bit port range of 65535) triggers a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating the port number is out of the valid 0-65535 range.
scenarios.injected_fault: TCP port number set to 70000 in the TCP profile configuration

scenarios.title: Boundary TCP Port Number Configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring a TCP profile with the maximum valid port number of 65535 is accepted as a valid boundary value.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is successfully validated with port 65535.

scenarios.title: Valid UDP Profile Configuration with Standard Options
scenarios.description: Verify that a UDP profile defined with valid UDPOption parameters (such as a valid destination port and no connection-oriented parameters) is successfully parsed.
scenarios.expected_result: The UDP profile is successfully parsed and registered in the communication configuration.

scenarios.title: Duplicate Channel Name Configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that defining two channels with the same identifier under communication/channels/ in FLYNCChannelConfig triggers a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a duplicate channel identifier error.
scenarios.injected_fault: Duplicate channel identifier defined in FLYNCChannelConfig

scenarios.title: Boundary TTL Hop Limit Configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring a TTL/Hop Limit at its maximum boundary value of 255 in the IP options is accepted, while 256 is rejected.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an out-of-range error for TTL/Hop Limit (must be 0-255).

scenarios.title: Valid ECU configuration
scenarios.description: Test that a valid ECU configuration is successfully loaded when containing the mandatory 'ports.flync.yaml' file and at least one controller directory under 'controllers/'.
scenarios.expected_result: ECU configuration loaded and validated successfully

scenarios.title: Invalid MDI configuration placement
scenarios.description: Test that defining an 'mdi_config' on a controller's Ethernet interface instead of the ECU Ports configuration raises a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Error: MDI configuration must be defined on ECU Ports, not on controller interfaces
scenarios.injected_fault: MDI configuration defined on controller interface

scenarios.title: VLAN ID upper boundary validation
scenarios.description: Test that a socket configuration with the maximum valid 802.1Q VLAN ID (4094) is successfully validated.
scenarios.expected_result: Socket configuration with VLAN ID 4094 validated successfully

scenarios.title: Valid socket configuration
scenarios.description: Test that a socket configuration file in the 'sockets/' directory successfully defines a group of sockets with a valid VLAN ID, IPv4 address endpoint, and port number.
scenarios.expected_result: Socket container configuration parsed and validated successfully

scenarios.title: Invalid VLAN ID out of bounds
scenarios.description: Test that a socket configuration with an out-of-bounds VLAN ID (4096) raises a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Error: VLAN ID must be in the range 1-4094

scenarios.title: Valid System Metadata Parsing
scenarios.description: Verify that a valid system_metadata.flync.yaml file containing mandatory system context and SemVer-compliant versioning is successfully parsed.
scenarios.expected_result: System metadata is successfully parsed and validated.

scenarios.title: System Metadata with PEP 440 Versioning
scenarios.description: Verify that system_metadata.flync.yaml is successfully parsed when using a complex PEP 440 version string (e.g., '1.2.3a1.post1') to test the boundary of the version parser.
scenarios.expected_result: System metadata is successfully parsed and PEP 440 version is validated.

scenarios.title: Valid ECU Metadata Parsing
scenarios.description: Verify that a valid ecu_metadata.flync.yaml file containing hardware and software metadata is successfully parsed.
scenarios.expected_result: ECU metadata is successfully parsed and validated.

scenarios.title: SocketsPerVLANMetadata with Invalid IP Address
scenarios.description: Verify that SocketsPerVLANMetadata is rejected when configured with an invalid IPv4 address containing an out-of-range octet.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails due to invalid IPv4 address format.

scenarios.title: SocketsPerVLANMetadata Port Number Boundary Check
scenarios.description: Verify that SocketsPerVLANMetadata validation fails when the port number is configured just outside the valid range of 0-65535.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails because the port number exceeds the maximum limit of 65535.

scenarios.title: Valid Group and Timing Profile Configuration
scenarios.description: A valid StateManagementGroup in groups.flync.yaml referencing a valid timing profile in timing_profiles.flync.yaml and a valid NM PDU.
scenarios.expected_result: Valid configuration

scenarios.title: Mixed CAN Bus Memberships
scenarios.description: A CAN bus configured with both node-level (ECU/controller) and bus-level state memberships, which must be rejected during validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Invalid configuration
scenarios.injected_fault: mixed node-level and bus-level memberships on the same CAN bus

scenarios.title: Participant Membership with Default Relevance Bit
scenarios.description: A participant state membership where relevance_bits is omitted, verifying that it successfully defaults to the declaring entity's name.
scenarios.expected_result: Valid configuration

scenarios.title: Invalid Timing Profile Reference
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup referencing a non-existent timing profile name, which must fail validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Invalid configuration

scenarios.title: Observer with Relevance Bits
scenarios.description: A state membership configured with role 'observer' that also declares relevance_bits, which must be rejected during validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Invalid configuration
scenarios.injected_fault: relevance_bits declared on an observer membership

scenarios.title: LIN Node-Level Membership
scenarios.description: Declaring node-level (ECU or controller) state membership for a LIN transport, which only supports bus-level membership.
scenarios.expected_result: Invalid configuration

scenarios.title: MACsec Configuration with Integrity and Confidentiality
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring MACsec with IntegrityWithConfidentiality successfully enables link-by-link Layer 2 encryption and integrity protection using MKA.
scenarios.expected_result: MACsec configuration is successfully applied with IntegrityWithConfidentiality enabled

scenarios.title: Invalid MACsec Key Length
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring MACsec with an invalid key length of 10 bytes is rejected, as MACsec requires 16-byte (128-bit) or 32-byte (256-bit) keys.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration is rejected because MACsec key length must be 16 or 32 bytes

scenarios.title: Duplicate Firewall Rule Configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring a Firewall with duplicate FirewallRule entries (matching protocol, source/destination IPs, and ports) is rejected.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration is rejected with an error indicating duplicate firewall rules are not allowed

scenarios.title: Firewall Rule with Boundary Port Numbers
scenarios.description: Verify that a FirewallRule with boundary port numbers (0 and 65535) is successfully validated.
scenarios.expected_result: Firewall rule with port 65535 is successfully validated

scenarios.title: Invalid Firewall Protocol
scenarios.description: Verify that a FirewallRule specifying an invalid or unsupported transport protocol is rejected.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration is rejected with an error indicating an invalid protocol

scenarios.title: Valid Signal with Text Table Encoding
scenarios.description: Verify that a UINT8 signal representing a gear selection can be successfully defined with a text_table value encoding mapping raw values 0-3 to Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive.
scenarios.expected_result: Signal is successfully validated with its text_table value encoding mapping raw values to labels.

scenarios.title: Invalid Signal with Non-Existent Data Type
scenarios.description: Verify that defining a signal with an invalid data_type string ('invalid_type') instead of a valid SignalDataType enum variant (such as 'UINT8') triggers a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating that 'invalid_type' is not a valid SignalDataType.

scenarios.title: Signal with Maximum Bit Length for UINT64
scenarios.description: Verify that a UINT64 signal can be defined with its maximum natural bit width of 64 bits.
scenarios.expected_result: Signal is successfully validated with a bit_length of 64 matching the natural bit width of UINT64.

scenarios.title: Invalid Signal with Duplicate Value Encoding
scenarios.description: Verify that a text_table value encoding with duplicate raw value entries (e.g., two entries mapping raw value 1 to different labels) is rejected during validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails due to duplicate value mapping or overlapping ranges in the text_table encoding.
scenarios.injected_fault: value_encoding: { type: text_table, entries: [{ value: 1, label: 'A' }, { value: 1, label: 'B' }] }

scenarios.title: Signal with Minimum Bit Length
scenarios.description: Verify that a signal can be defined with the minimum bit length of 1 bit using the UINT8 data type.
scenarios.expected_result: Signal is successfully validated with a bit_length of 1.

scenarios.title: Invalid Signal with Missing Bit Length
scenarios.description: Verify that a signal definition missing the mandatory bit_length field is rejected during validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails indicating that bit_length is a required field and cannot be null.

scenarios.title: Valid SOME/IP Service Interface Configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that a valid SOMEIPServiceInterface configuration containing a unique Service Identifier, a SOMEIPRequestResponseMethod, a SOMEIPEvent, and a SOMEIPEventgroup is successfully parsed and instantiated.
scenarios.expected_result: The SOMEIPServiceInterface is successfully instantiated with the defined methods, events, and eventgroups.

scenarios.title: Duplicate Service ID in SOME/IP Service Interface
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring two SOMEIPServiceInterface instances with the same unique Service Identifier within the same SOMEIPConfig deployment results in a validation error.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating duplicate Service Identifier.

scenarios.title: Boundary SOME/IP Service ID and Method ID Values
scenarios.description: Verify that a SOMEIPServiceInterface with the maximum valid 16-bit Service ID (65535) and a SOMEIPMethod with the maximum valid Method ID (32767) are successfully parsed.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is successfully validated and instantiated with boundary ID values.

scenarios.title: Invalid SOME/IP Datatype in Service Interface
scenarios.description: Verify that a SOMEIPParameter configured with an invalid or unsupported datatype (not defined in someip_datatypes) is rejected during validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating an unsupported or invalid SOME/IP datatype.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP TP Activation Threshold Boundary
scenarios.description: Verify that SOMEIPTP segmentation activates exactly when the payload size exceeds the configured UDP segment size threshold by 1 byte, and remains inactive when it is exactly equal to the threshold.
scenarios.expected_result: SOME/IP TP is triggered only when the payload exceeds the threshold, and standard UDP deployment is used when payload is equal to or below the threshold.

scenarios.title: Valid System Topology with Multiple ECUs
scenarios.description: Verify a valid system topology with multiple ECUs where all external connections are of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'.
scenarios.expected_result: No errors, valid system topology

scenarios.title: Invalid System Topology with Duplicate ECU ID
scenarios.description: Verify that the system topology parser rejects configurations containing duplicate ECU identifiers.
scenarios.expected_result: Error: Duplicate ECU ID found in system topology

scenarios.title: System Topology with a Single ECU
scenarios.description: Verify the boundary condition of a system topology containing exactly one ECU, where no external connections are specified.
scenarios.expected_result: No errors, valid single-ECU system topology

scenarios.title: Invalid External Connection Type
scenarios.description: Verify that an external connection with a type other than 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' is rejected.
scenarios.expected_result: Error: Connection type must be 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'

scenarios.title: External Connection Referencing Non-Existent ECU
scenarios.description: Verify that an external connection referencing an ECU ID not defined in the system topology is rejected as a dangling reference.
scenarios.expected_result: Error: Referenced ECU ID not found in system topology
scenarios.injected_fault: Dangling ECU reference in external connection

scenarios.title: Valid gPTP configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that a PTPConfig containing a PTPPort configured with PTPTimeTransmitterConfig and PTPPdelayConfig is successfully parsed and validated.
scenarios.expected_result: PTPConfig is successfully validated

scenarios.title: Conflicting PTP port roles
scenarios.description: Verify that configuring a PTPPort with both PTPTimeTransmitterConfig and PTPTimeReceiverConfig simultaneously is rejected by the validator.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a configuration error
scenarios.injected_fault: Conflicting transmitter and receiver configurations on a single port

scenarios.title: CBS shaper credit boundary validation
scenarios.description: Verify that a CBSShaper configuration with highCredit and lowCredit set to their maximum and minimum allowed integer limits is successfully validated.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration is successfully validated and applied

scenarios.title: Valid traffic class configuration
scenarios.description: Verify that a TrafficClass configuration containing a valid CBSShaper and mapped to a specific egress queue is successfully validated.
scenarios.expected_result: TrafficClass is successfully created and mapped to the egress queue

scenarios.title: Invalid CBS shaper idleSlope
scenarios.description: Verify that a CBSShaper configuration is rejected when the idleSlope exceeds the physical link speed of the port.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an idleSlope out of bounds error

scenarios.title: DoubleRateThreeColorMarker boundary validation
scenarios.description: Verify that a DoubleRateThreeColorMarker configuration where the Peak Information Rate (PIR) is set exactly equal to the Committed Information Rate (CIR) is successfully validated.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration is successfully validated with PIR equal to CIR

scenarios.title: ContainerPDU Size Overflowing UDP Socket Buffer Configuration
scenarios.description: A ContainerPDU defined in flync_4_communication aggregates multiple independent PDUs containing high-frequency signals defined in flync_4_signal. This ContainerPDU is routed to an Ethernet socket on a target ECU configured in flync_4_ecu. The test checks the system's behavior when the cumulative size of the contained PDUs exceeds the maximum UDP socket buffer size (UDPOption) configured for the target ECU port.
scenarios.expected_result: The validation engine flags a configuration mismatch error, indicating that the maximum possible size of the ContainerPDU exceeds the UDPOption buffer size of the receiving ECU socket.
scenarios.injected_fault: The combined payload size of the contained PDUs in the ContainerPDU configuration exceeds the 'max_packet_size' or buffer limits defined in the target ECU's UDPOption.

scenarios.title: End-to-End CAN FD Frame and Signal Mapping to ECU Controller
scenarios.description: A CAN FD Frame is defined in flync_4_communication with Bit Rate Switch (BRS) enabled and a payload of 64 bytes. It contains a SignalInstance wrapping a 32-bit float signal from flync_4_signal. This frame is mapped to a CAN FD controller configured on a specific ECU in flync_4_ecu.
scenarios.expected_result: Successful generation of the network description (e.g., ARXML or DBC) with correct bit-mappings, controller settings, and BRS flags aligned across all submodels.

scenarios.title: SecOC PDU Freshness Value and MAC Bit-Width Alignment
scenarios.description: A secured PDU (SecOC) is configured in flync_4_communication to protect a critical control signal from flync_4_signal. The target ECU in flync_4_ecu must process this. The test verifies the boundary condition where the combined bit-widths of the payload signal, the Message Authentication Code (MAC), and the Freshness Value exactly equal the maximum payload limit of the underlying Classic CAN frame (8 bytes / 64 bits).
scenarios.expected_result: The system validates that the total bit-width is exactly 64 bits, allowing successful compilation without triggering truncation or padding errors.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP Multicast Event Group Port Mismatch
scenarios.description: A SOME/IP service event group is configured in flync_4_communication to use IP multicast for dynamic service discovery (SOME/IP-SD). The subscriber ECU is configured in flync_4_ecu with a physical ECUPort. The test checks if the system detects when the subscriber ECU's port configuration lacks multicast capability or has mismatched MDI/MII configurations that prevent multicast routing.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation failure during configuration compilation, highlighting that the subscriber ECU port cannot join the multicast group specified in the SOME/IP-SD configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: The subscriber ECU's port configuration in ports.flync.yaml does not support multicast routing, but the communication channel config assigns it to a multicast group.
